mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% annualized coincides with higher corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of strong GDPC1 acceleration (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals labor market overheating, which raises inflation and discount rate expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE < 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -2% annualized indicates weakening manufacturing demand, which reduces earnings growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of INDPRO < -2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of FEDFUNDS > 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below -2% annualized indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of GDPC1 < -2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market slack, which reduces wage pressures and supports lower discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of UNRATE > 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% and a 3-month increase in average hourly earnings (PAYEMS) above 4% annualized signals labor market overheating, which raises inflation and discount rate expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 4% annualized for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 4% (t-test p > 0.05).
